budget_tradeoff_detail: HCP compresses full-repository context from 50,000+ tokens to ~8,000 tokens while improving EM by roughly 3-6 points across six Code LLMs (DeepseekCoder, Starcoder2, CodeGemma variants).
confound_note: Headline comparison (Random-All baseline vs HCP) varies both representation (flat concatenation vs hierarchical dependency-graph+embedding pruning) and token budget (~50k vs ~8k) simultaneously; secondary ablations (Table 2 dependency-level D1..Dinf, Table 3 pruning-level P0-P2) hold the max context window fixed while varying representation/pruning depth, giving a budget-matched comparison for those specific tables.
stop_detail: Builds a function/class/file dependency graph via Tree-Sitter import parsing with BFS dependency levels D0..Dinf, then uses embedding-based top-k/top-p similarity ranking to select and prune function bodies (full content for current file, headers-only for low-relevance functions elsewhere), assembled hierarchically at prompt-construction time (Sec. 3, 'Hierarchical Context Pruning').
threats_to_datum: Extracted via WebFetch-rendered HTML rather than the original PDF; exact table/figure numbers should be spot-checked against the PDF source before final reporting.

demote_reason: Full text (arxiv.org/html/2502.17139) shows FastCoder's retrieval targets speculative-decoding draft token sequences from a context-continuation datastore (repository-specific + general Stack-derived), used purely to accelerate autoregressive generation via tree-attention verification. It does not construct, structure, or budget cross-file repository context for the LLM's input prompt — no file/function selection, no token-budget management for context inclusion is discussed anywhere in the paper. The paper's own contribution is inference-latency acceleration (up to 2.53x speedup on RepoEval), not context representation.

stop_detail: Builds a Repository Structural Semantic Graph (RSSG) over classes/functions/attributes via Pytype+Tree-sitter static analysis, retrieves four context views (caller functions, DFS-predicted callee call chains, embedding-similar functions, similar code fragments), then serializes them into a structure-preserving prompt under a two-stage per-view token budget capped at 4096 tokens (RSSG Construction / Call Chain Prediction / Prompt Construction sections); explicitly a static one-shot pipeline with no agentic tool use or multi-turn LLM queries.

key_numbers.metric: Qwen2.5-Coder-14B EM (V/SV), fine-tuned+retrieval
Fixed input context window across all evaluated models/methods
Pre-trained baseline EM before fine-tuning

budget_tradeoff_detail: A fixed 2,048-token input window is used uniformly across all models and retrieval baselines (RepoCoder, GraphCoder, RLCoder); when repository context exceeds this, head/tail truncation is applied, and retrieval methods select which cross-file snippets fill the remaining budget instead — GraphCoder notably underperforms on hardware languages despite the same fixed budget.
confound_note: The central comparison (raw truncated whole-file concatenation vs. RepoCoder/GraphCoder/RLCoder retrieval-augmented context) holds the 2,048-token budget fixed while varying only the representation/retrieval mechanism used to select cross-file content — a budget-matched representation ablation; however the headline Table 5 numbers combine this with model fine-tuning, so representation and fine-tuning effects are not cleanly separated in the top-line results.
stop_detail: Cross-file repository context is built by concatenating whole files under '--- FILE: path (BEGIN) ---' delimiters up to a fixed 2,048-token window with head/tail truncation when over budget, optionally replaced by retrieval-augmented snippets from RepoCoder/GraphCoder/RLCoder baselines evaluated on the benchmark.
threats_to_datum: Read via WebFetch's rendered HTML of arXiv v2 (Feb 2026), not the original PDF; could not confirm from the fetched text exactly which retrieval method paired with the headline Qwen2.5-Coder-14B result, so mechanism/representation attribution for that specific number should be checked against the PDF tables.

demote_reason: Full text (arxiv.org/html/2602.11988, Sec. 3-4) confirms the manipulated variable is presence/absence and provenance (LLM-generated vs. developer-committed) of a single free-text repository documentation file (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md containing repo overview, tooling, build/test commands, style guides), not a structural representation of the repository code. No AST, call/dependency graph, CPG, embedding retrieval, or repo-map construction is used anywhere; evaluation is behavioral (tool-call traces, step counts, reasoning tokens) rather than a comparison of code-context representations under a held structural budget. The reported +20% inference-cost figure (Table 2) is a side-effect of documentation-file length/injection, not a budget-matched ablation of a cross-file structural context representation, so this falls outside the SLR scope on structure-aware context engineering.

Full text (arxiv.org/html/2605.05400) confirms this is a purely prescriptive human workflow methodology for preparing markdown briefing documents and task-decomposition records BEFORE invoking a coding agent — paper states 'MEP operates at workflow rather than invocation scope.' There is no automated mechanism for parsing, representing, retrieving, compressing, or budgeting existing repository code content (no AST, call graph, embedding retrieval, repo map, or agentic exploration of code) — no code instantiation of a context-representation system exists. Also secondarily fails E4 (no cross-file structural token/cost budget is discussed anywhere). Empirical support is a single uncontrolled hackathon case study (Section 4), not a benchmark/ablation.

demote_reason: Full text (arxiv.org/html/2607.27250, Sec 3-5) shows the three ablated arms (none / always_on / selective) all vary only the DELIVERY of a free-text documentation file (AGENTS.md or topic-organized wiki pages read on demand) — the paper states this 'vary[ies] primarily how context is delivered.' No AST, call/dependency graph, code-property graph, embedding retrieval, or repo-map representation of the repository's code is ever constructed or compared, and no token-budget-vs-quality tradeoff over such a representation is studied (only operational cost caps like '$6/run' and turn limits are reported, not a budget-matched representation ablation). The central comparison is presence/type of a natural-language guidance artifact, not a cross-file structural code-context budgeting concern.
